{{estvisual:quality}}
Worked comparison · Same estimate, different precision

The same estimate can come from different-quality rules

Return to the five orders $46, $52, $48, $54 and $50. Compare two rules chosen before seeing their values: average all five orders, or average only the first and fourth. Both happen to give $50 today. Does that make the rules equally precise?

Compare the sampling rules, not just today’s answer{{math:depth-fixed-weight-comparison}}

Under IID sampling with a common finite variance σ², both rules are unbiased: their fixed weights sum to 1. But the two-order rule has 2.5 times the variance of the five-order mean, because half of σ² is 2.5 times one fifth of σ². Its standard error is √2.5 ≈ 1.5811 times as large.

The business paid to collect five orders; the second rule discards the information in three of them. Equality of today’s answers does not remove that loss. Choosing which orders to include after looking at their values is a different, data-dependent rule and is not covered by this fixed-weight proof.

The full derivation below extends the comparison to any fixed weights summing to 1. Equal weights attain the smallest variance in that class under the stated common-variance, independence assumptions.
